explanation: A reflection on success from Stillwords.

text: Build your house on the rock of daily integrity, not on the shifting sand of momentary applause.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on success from Stillwords.

text: Measure success by how few things you need to be content, not by how many you have accumulated.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on success from Stillwords.

text: When you reach the top of the ridge, reach your hand down to pull up the person behind you.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on success from Stillwords.

text: Success is falling seven times and getting up eight with an intact sense of humor.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on success from Stillwords.

text: Do good work every day and let the reputation take care of itself.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on success from Stillwords.

text: The fruit of true success is not wealth; it is freedom over your own hours and peace in your thoughts.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on success from Stillwords.

text: Celebrate every small milestone along the trail. The summit is only one step of a thousand.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on success from Stillwords.

text: Never sacrifice your health or your family on the altar of commercial success.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on success from Stillwords.

text: Patience and persistence are the quiet twin engines of every lasting triumph.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on success from Stillwords.

text: Be reliable. In a world full of flaky promises, the person who does what they said they would do is legendary.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on success from Stillwords.

text: Leave every client, reader, or colleague better off than when you first met them.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on success from Stillwords.

text: You do not need to cut corners to succeed. The straight path is less crowded anyway.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on success from Stillwords.

text: Success is turning your wound into wisdom and your struggle into service.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on success from Stillwords.

text: Keep your overhead low and your craftsmanship high. That is the secret of independence.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on success from Stillwords.

text: The greatest reward of your labor is not what you get for it, but what you become by it.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on success from Stillwords.

text: Do not let success go to your head or failure go to your heart. Stay balanced on both feet.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on success from Stillwords.

text: Live so that those who know you best respect you most.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on success from Stillwords.

text: Success is waking up with excitement for the work and going to sleep with satisfaction for the day.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on success from Stillwords.

text: Never compromise your honor to secure a contract. Money returns; a broken name does not.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on success from Stillwords.

text: True abundance is having enough to share with someone whose cupboard is bare.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on success from Stillwords.

text: Treat triumph and setback as two impostors of equal insignificance compared to character.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on success from Stillwords.

text: A successful life is simply a string of honest, well-lived days tied together with love.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on success from Stillwords.

text: Dwell on the beauty of life. Watch the stars, and see yourself running with them.
author: Marcus Aurelius
explanation: A reflection on wisdom from Stillwords.

text: Wisdom is knowing what to overlook. Life is too short to engage with every provocation.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on wisdom from Stillwords.

text: The quietest man in the room often carries the heaviest cargo of understanding.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on wisdom from Stillwords.

text: Do not confuse knowledge with wisdom. One is acquiring tools; the other is knowing when to leave them in the box.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on wisdom from Stillwords.

text: Look at the night sky. In that immense silence, all our petty anxieties shrink to their proper size.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on wisdom from Stillwords.

text: The river cuts through rock not because of violence, but because of patient, unyielding persistence.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on wisdom from Stillwords.

text: Speak only when your words are more beneficial than the silence they replace.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on wisdom from Stillwords.

text: To be at peace with your own mortality is to receive every single morning as a priceless miracle.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on wisdom from Stillwords.

text: He who angers you conquers you. Keep your composure and keep your crown.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on wisdom from Stillwords.

text: Listen to the counsel of old trees: dig deep roots, bend with winter gales, and offer shade freely.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on wisdom from Stillwords.

text: A wise person builds bridges out of stones that other people throw at them.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on wisdom from Stillwords.

text: Do not cross a deep river on rumors of shallow water. Check the current with your own staff.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on wisdom from Stillwords.

text: The greatest prison you will ever inhabit is fear of what other people think of you. Walk out the door.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on wisdom from Stillwords.

text: True wealth is not having overflowing barns, but having an unburdened spirit that owes nothing to vanity.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on wisdom from Stillwords.

text: Let time be your filter. What seems like an emergency at three in the afternoon is often forgotten by sunrise.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on wisdom from Stillwords.

text: A clean heart and clear eyes are the two greatest compasses for any human pilgrimage.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on wisdom from Stillwords.

text: Do not judge the quality of a life by its length, but by the depth of love it contained.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on wisdom from Stillwords.

text: Sit with the wise in silence; their stillness will teach you more than twenty arguments.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on wisdom from Stillwords.

text: Everything in nature yields to its proper season. Do not demand summer in the dead of January.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on wisdom from Stillwords.

text: The tongue is a small rudder that can wreck a magnificent ship. Steer it with vigilance.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on wisdom from Stillwords.

text: He who knows when he has enough is rich beyond the counting of gold coins.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on wisdom from Stillwords.

text: Forgive the debts of the past. The ledger of bitterness will only poison the accountant.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on wisdom from Stillwords.

text: Patience is not passive waiting; it is active calm while the seeds do their invisible work.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on wisdom from Stillwords.

text: Look upon your enemies with compassion. Hurt people hurt people; healed people bring medicine.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on wisdom from Stillwords.

text: The greatest wisdom is to remain gentle in a world that prides itself on hardness.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on wisdom from Stillwords.

text: Do not measure your worth by the applause of a crowd that will forget you by twilight.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on wisdom from Stillwords.

text: Hold onto what is good with a steady grip, and release the rest without rancor.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on wisdom from Stillwords.

text: The stars do not compete with one another; each shines in its assigned quadrant of the night.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on wisdom from Stillwords.

text: A wise person finds a teacher in every experience, even in painful ones.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on wisdom from Stillwords.

text: Live simply, speak honestly, and leave a trail of gentle peace wherever your boots tread.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on wisdom from Stillwords.

text: Craftsmanship is love made visible in wood, stone, ink, or code.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on work from Stillwords.

text: Do not rush the joint that holds the roof up. Take the extra hour to make it true.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on work from Stillwords.

text: Work with clean hands and a steady heart. The work you leave behind is your signature on reality.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on work from Stillwords.

text: Sweep the floor of your shop as if an emperor were visiting. Dignity lives in every square inch.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on work from Stillwords.

text: Clear the table of distractions. One clear task tackled with full focus will move mountains.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on work from Stillwords.

text: Do not let haste ruin what patience was meant to perfect.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on work from Stillwords.

text: Honest labor sweetens the evening crust of bread and softens the nighttime pillow.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on work from Stillwords.

text: Take pride in the invisible infrastructure you build that nobody will ever notice until it fails.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on work from Stillwords.

text: Show up on time, speak plainly, and deliver what you promised. That is nine-tenths of genius.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on work from Stillwords.

text: Treat your tools with care. A sharp chisel saves the carpenter an entire afternoon of bruised timber.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on work from Stillwords.

text: Let your work be an offering to the common good, not just a transaction for survival.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on work from Stillwords.

text: Do not complain about the grain of the wood. The master woodworker adapts the chisel to the knot.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on work from Stillwords.

text: A difficult problem yields to patient dismantling piece by piece. Start with the easiest bolt.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on work from Stillwords.

text: Rest when the job is done, but never while your hand is on the plow.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on work from Stillwords.

text: Find quiet pleasure in the smell of sawdust, the hum of the engine, the tap of keys.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on work from Stillwords.

text: When you build something solid, you leave an anchor in the storm for someone who comes after you.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on work from Stillwords.

text: Never compromise on safety or truth to speed up delivery.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on work from Stillwords.

text: The artisan's highest reward is standing back at sunset and knowing: 'I built that with care.'
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on work from Stillwords.

text: Do not let commercial pressure extinguish the artistic soul of your labor.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on work from Stillwords.

text: Work side by side with good people. Shared toil builds bonds that time cannot corrode.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on work from Stillwords.

text: Every profession is honorable when practiced with clean motives and deep attention.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on work from Stillwords.

text: Learn the fundamentals backwards and forwards. True freedom in craft begins with mastery of basics.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on work from Stillwords.

text: A day of honest labor brings a night of deep, untroubled slumber.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on work from Stillwords.

text: Treat your coworkers with gentle dignity, especially on the days when deadlines pinch.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on work from Stillwords.

text: Do not leave a job half-done. Finish the row so tomorrow's sunrise greets an open field.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on work from Stillwords.

text: The greatest tribute to your trade is teaching its secrets to the next generation.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on work from Stillwords.

text: Work with joy. Bitterness in labor poisons both the maker and the object made.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on work from Stillwords.

text: Measure twice, cut once: that is the golden rule of carpentry and human speech alike.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on work from Stillwords.

text: A well-crafted life is your greatest masterpiece. Give it your highest craftsmanship.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on work from Stillwords.

text: Put your hand to the work with gladness today. You have an opportunity to leave the world better.
author: Stillwords
explanation: A reflection on work from Stillwords.
